land.text: the Garamantian kingdom of the Fezzan, roughly 180,000 km2 on the Garamantes page, taken by Uqba ibn Nafi

successors.note: Uqba took Germa and Waddan in the 660s (663 on the Battle of Germa infobox, 666/7 on the conquest page); the Garamantes page puts the end of the civilisation in the late 7th century AD.

capitals.name: Garama (Germa, Jarma)
capitals.note: 'their largest town, Garama'. The page says 'an earlier capital, Zinkekara, was located not far from the later Garama' but dates neither the move nor the capital's start, so one entry spans the life of the state; Garama's coordinates are the gazetteer's for Germa.

correction.text: the oasis core around Garama (Germa), the Wadi al-Ajal, the Fezzan oases the Garamantes had settled 'at least as early as 1000 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page dates the settlement (1000 BC), the first written record (5th century BC, Herodotus) and the rise to 'a major regional power in the mid-2nd century AD', and gives no extent before then, so the early shape is only the oasis core (radius 120 km, my reading). A footnote claims a 'powerful polity' from the 6th century BCE; the page contradicts itself on the start.

correction.text: a kingdom that 'spanned roughly 180,000 km2 in the Fezzan region of southern Libya', with Ghat and Barkat as key southern oases

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. A 240 km circle around Garama is 181,000 km2, the page's figure; the Fezzan region of the gazetteer (510,000 km2) is the whole Sabha and Murzuq districts and too large. Ends with the Arab conquest of the 660s.

region.text: the oasis core around Garama (Germa) in the Fezzan

ledger.note: 500 BCE (approx.): the Garamantes are the people of the Fezzan oases around Garama. 'The earliest known written record to document the Garamantes dates to the 5th century BC' (Herodotus); the page is silent on any founding of a state and a footnote puts a 'powerful polity' in the 6th century BCE, so the year is a bracket, not a date.

region.text: a kingdom spanning roughly 180,000 km2 in the Fezzan region, with Ghat and Barkat as southern oases

ledger.note: c.150: the Garamantes become a major power. 'The Garamantes first emerged as a major regional power in the mid-2nd century AD' in a kingdom 'that spanned roughly 180,000 km2 in the Fezzan region'; the year rounds 'mid-2nd century' and the footprint is my reading of the area figure.

region.text: the Garamantian kingdom of the Fezzan: Germa, Waddan and the oases taken by Uqba ibn Nafi

ledger.note: 666: Uqba ibn Nafi takes the Fezzan for the caliphate. Conquest page: Uqba 'returned to the Fezzan and took Waddan' after 663 and is placed in the Fezzan taking Germa around the 666/7 raids; the Uqba page gives 'In 46 AH / 666 CE' for Waddan and lists a 'Battle of Germa (663)' in its infobox. The Garamantes page says only that the civilisation lasted 'until its end in the late 7th century AD', so 666 is the conquest, not the last trace.

wars.name: Roman expeditions against the Garamantes (19 BC, 50 AD)
wars.outcome: Raids without a lasting border change: 'Lucius Cornelius Balbus and other Romans captured fifteen of their settlements in 19 BC'; the Fezzan page names 'Septimus Flaccus in 19 BCE and Suetonius Paulinus in 50 CE' for the 'small-scale military expeditions'.
wars.note: The page records no Roman occupation, tribute or garrison; the two pages disagree on the general of 19 BC (Balbus on the Garamantes page, Septimus Flaccus on the Fezzan page). Valerius Festus's campaign (the Garamantes buried their wells and ambushed the Romans, 'who retreated') is undated on the page and not entered.

wars.name: War of Oea and Leptis Magna
wars.outcome: 'In 69 AD the Garamantes would support Oea against Leptis Magna'; no change of border recorded.

wars.name: Septimius Severus's capture of Garama
wars.outcome: 'In 202 AD, Septimius Severus captured the capital city of Garama.' The page does not say how long Rome held it or whether the kingdom lost land, so no border change is entered.

wars.name: Arab conquest of the Fezzan
wars.outcome: The Garamantian kingdom falls to Uqba ibn Nafi: Germa and Waddan taken in the 660s ('Battle of Germa (663)' in the Uqba page's infobox; Waddan '46 AH / 666 CE' in its text; the conquest page puts the Germa operation around the 666/7 raids).
wars.note: The dates differ by page (663 versus 666/7); the dossier ends the state in 666. No contest events are entered because the pages describe raids, not a held front.

certainty.note: Oasis-centred polity in the Sahara: no frontier is described on any page; the 180,000 km2 figure is an area, not a boundary.

notes: Cliopatria has no Garamantes row (polities.csv). Start year is a bracket: the page puts the earliest written record in the 5th century BC (Herodotus), a footnote asserts a powerful polity from the 6th century BCE, and the lead says the kingdom 'first emerged as a major regional power in the mid-2nd century AD'. The page has no infobox in the fetched text and names only one king (Masyphios, undated). The end year is the Arab conquest of the Fezzan (663 or 666/7 depending on the page); the Garamantes page speaks of a 'late 7th century AD' end of the civilisation. The Garamantian hold on Ghat and the Wadi al-Ajal after 666 is not on the pages. Gazetteer: Germa, Fezzan and Ghat resolve; the radii are mine. Roman events are entered in wars only because no page gives a held front. A gap-filler could open 'Cornelius Balbus', 'Roman Libya' or 'Septimius Severus' for the garrisons (Bu Njem) the Garamantes page does not mention.
